implementation_notes: Scala has no lock-free queue in its own standard library; on the JVM the realization is the JDK class - ConcurrentLinkedQueue (documented non-blocking MPMC) used directly, with scala.jdk.CollectionConverters providing a Scala view when for-comprehensions or combinators are wanted. For asynchronous pipelines the idiomatic replacement is a higher-level effect or actor queue (fs2, cats-effect Queue, Akka/Pekko streams): those add backpressure and completion semantics, although their internals are not the CAS structure. Scala Native and Scala.js have no java.util.concurrent, so shared code needs a platform-specific structure or plain message passing.
code_sketch:
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue
import scala.jdk.CollectionConverters.*
val q = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue[Job]
q.offer(job)                          // non-blocking
val next = Option(q.poll())           // null -> None when empty
q.asScala.foreach(process)            // Scala view of a weakly consistent iterator
pitfalls: poll() returns null and Scala's type system does not force a check - wrap the result in Option immediately.
asScala is only a wrapper: iteration stays weakly consistent, so it must not be treated as a snapshot.
Scala.js and Scala Native lack the JDK queue entirely; do not let the JVM realization leak into shared sources.
